question: How do we decide when a task deserves the most powerful AI and when a simpler one is enough?
reflection: Choosing the right tool for each job saves resources that can be shared more widely, which is progress in itself.

sources.subject: The missing middleware: Why AI at scale requires model routers

one_line: Model routers, which send each request to the cheapest model that can handle it, are becoming a standard part of large AI systems.

top_stories.title: Why routers sit between apps and models
top_stories.what: The newsletter argues that open models can handle most routine requests and that a router should send only hard cases to expensive top models, using rules, learned classifiers, cheap-first cascades or blends of several models.
top_stories.why: Routing is a practical way to keep large analysis projects affordable without lowering quality where it matters.

top_stories.title: Commercial routing services
top_stories.what: OpenRouter offers a router that blends answers from several cheaper models and reportedly beat single top models on a research benchmark at about half the cost; Not Diamond trains custom routers on a team's own test data.
top_stories.why: Managed routers lower the effort needed to use several models at once.

top_stories.title: Open-source routers for private setups
top_stories.what: Open tools such as NadirClaw and ACRouter run locally; ACRouter learns from checked results over time to improve its choices.
top_stories.why: Self-hosted routing keeps prompts and data inside the organisation, which suits strict data rules.

saudi_lens.text: Routing most work to open models hosted locally, and only rare cases to foreign cloud models, is one way Saudi organisations can balance cost with data residency rules.

idea.title: Build an evaluation set first
idea.pitch: Before choosing AI models for a project, collect a small set of real tasks with agreed correct answers so any model or router can be tested fairly.
idea.first_step: Gather 30 past tasks with known good outputs and store them in one shared folder.

idea_kids.title: Which tool for the job?
idea_kids.pitch: A sorting game where children match everyday tasks to the simplest tool that works, such as a ruler, a calculator or asking an adult.
idea_kids.first_step: Make twenty task cards and six tool cards from cardboard.

terms.definition: Automatically sending each AI request to the model best suited to it by cost, speed and difficulty.
Running software on your own servers instead of using a provider's cloud service.
Examples kept aside and never used in building a system, so they give an honest measure of how well it works.

concepts.summary: Routers send easy requests to cheap models and hard ones to top models.
Blends of cheaper models can match single top models at lower cost.
